claims.claim: The energy in the sunlight on your skin spent tens of thousands of years, maybe far more, getting out of the Sun.
claims.source_checked: NASA SVS 11084 'Origin of Light' (fetched with the CA bundle); Mitalas & Sills 1992 ApJ 401, 759 (NASA ADS scan, both pages); NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior' (solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml); Crossref records for doi:10.1086/172103 and doi:10.1023/A:1022952621810
claims.note: SVS: 'Over the course of 40,000 years it will be absorbed by other atoms and emitted repeatedly until reaching the sun's surface' (also image caption 'Over tens of thousands of years ... drunken walk'). MS92 abstract and sec. 3: t_d = 1.7 x 10^5 yr to the inner edge of the convective zone; the common 3e3-3e4 yr is 'much too short'. MSFC: 'about a million years to finally reach the interface layer'. Every source read gives >= 4e4 yr, and the convection leg only adds time, so 'tens of thousands, maybe far more' holds; 'far more' rests on MSFC (read), not on Stix (unread). 'Energy' rather than 'photon' is a fair paraphrase: SVS and MSFC both describe absorption and re-emission, i.e. the energy, not one particle, makes the trip. Pedant risk, not a break: beyond the factor 3 in MS92 eq. 2 already noted in SOURCES, MS92 also take each step equal to the local mean free path, while exponentially distributed free paths give <l^2> = 2 l^2; both together would lower 1.7e5 to about 2.8e4 yr, still tens of thousands. A1: SOURCES item 2.

claims.claim: First-sentence / swipe-at-two-seconds reading (A4): by 2.0 s the viewer has heard 'The energy in the sunlight on your skin' over the Sun-Earth shot with a pulse crossing and Earth labelled 'not to scale'; the full first sentence (to 6.2 s) says the energy took tens of thousands of years or more to get out of the Sun.
claims.source_checked: src/generated/age-of-sunlight.alignment.json word timings; src/shorts/age-of-sunlight/index.tsx (Pulse at frames 6-106 at 30 fps, Earth label opacity tied to Earth); sources as in claim 1
claims.note: At 2 s nothing numeric has been said, so nothing false is carried away. The first sentence alone is true as stated (claim 1) and avoids the popular false form ('the photon hitting you is 100,000 years old'). Minor pedant risk only: the first pulse reaches Earth at ~3.5 s, while 'tens of thousands of years' is spoken (2.7-3.9 s); the sentence finishes 'getting out of the Sun' by 6.2 s and the visual itself carries no time label, so no false claim is shown.

claims.claim: The trip from the Sun to you took eight minutes.
claims.source_checked: NASA NSSDC Sun fact sheet (radius 695,700 km; Earth distance mean 149.6, min 147.1, max 152.1 x 10^6 km); NIST CODATA 2022 c = 299 792 458 m/s exact; NASA SVS 11084
claims.note: (149.6e9 - 0.6957e9) m / c = 496.7 s = 8 min 17 s; range 8.14-8.42 min from perihelion to aphelion. SVS caption: 'Light takes eight minutes to travel the 93 million miles from the sun to Earth.' 'Eight minutes' is the rounding NASA itself uses (A3). IAU 2012 B2 was not reachable, but the claim does not need it: the NSSDC mean distance gives the same answer. A1: SOURCES item 1.

claims.claim: Getting out was the slow part.
claims.note: 8 min against >= 4e4 yr. No new figure. A1: SOURCES item 3.

claims.claim: But it is not the same light.
claims.source_checked: NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior'; NASA SVS 11084
claims.note: MSFC: energy crosses the radiative zone as radiation, 'mostly gamma-rays and x-rays', and the core's reactions release 'the energy that ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'. SVS: each photon is 'absorbed by other atoms and emitted repeatedly'. Either reading (different kind of light, or not the same photons) is supported. A1: SOURCES item 4.

claims.claim: Deep inside, it travels mostly as X-rays.
claims.source_checked: NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior' (centre ~15,000,000 C; radiative zone 7,000,000 C falling to ~2,000,000 C); NIST CODATA 2022 Wien wavelength displacement constant 2.897 771 955e-3 m K (exact); NASA NSSDC Sun fact sheet (central temperature 1.571e7 K)
claims.note: MSFC says 'mostly gamma-rays and x-rays'; the narrower 'mostly X-rays' (A3) follows from MSFC's own temperatures: Wien peak photon energy hc T / b = 6.4, 3.0, 0.86 keV at 15, 7, 2 MK (frequency peak 2.821 kT = 3.6, 1.7, 0.49 keV), all X-ray; recomputed and they match SOURCES item 4. The Planck tails make it 'mostly' by a wide margin: well under 1% of the energy is above 100 keV, and about 1% is below 0.1 keV even at 2 MK. Gamma rays come from the reactions themselves (MSFC pp chain), which the script does not deny. A1: SOURCES item 4.

claims.claim: It leaves as sunlight.
claims.note: MSFC: 'the energy that ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'; surface 5,700 K. A1: SOURCES item 4.

claims.claim: The energy is ancient.
claims.note: Characterisation of >= 4e4 yr (up to ~1e6 yr per MSFC); no new figure. A1: SOURCES item 5.

claims.claim: Its last eight minutes were the trip to you.
claims.note: Surface-to-Earth light time 8.1-8.4 min; SVS 'Light takes eight minutes'. A1: SOURCES items 1 and 5.

claims.claim: Sun-Earth shot with a bright pulse crossing the gap; Earth labelled 'not to scale' for as long as it is visible (start and end of the short).
claims.where: on-screen: Sun-Earth shot / 'not to scale' under Earth
claims.source_checked: src/shorts/age-of-sunlight/index.tsx (label opacity uses the same 'earth' value as the Earth body); NSSDC fact sheet
claims.note: A6 met: the shot is deliberately not to scale (code: Earth ~25x too big, ~40x too close) and says so whenever Earth is drawn. The pulse depicts light crossing from the Sun's surface to Earth, which is what the script says. A1: SOURCES item 6.

claims.claim: 8 MINUTES / surface to your skin / not to scale
claims.note: Photosphere to Earth 496.7 s mean (8 min 17 s), 8.1-8.4 min over the year; '8 minutes' is NASA's own rounding. A1: SOURCES item 1.

claims.claim: 10,000+ YEARS / energy, core to surface / not to scale (shown while the interior cutaway is up)
claims.source_checked: As claim 1; index.tsx timing (tag from F.rest to F.ancient+48; cutaway opacity is non-zero only over the same span)
claims.note: A lower bound, weaker than the spoken 'tens of thousands', and true for every source read: SVS 4e4 to the surface; MS92 1.7e5 and MSFC ~1e6 to the base of the convection zone, with convection adding a little more. The tag's 'not to scale' covers the cutaway for its whole time on screen (A6). A1: SOURCES item 2 ('On screen: 10,000+ YEARS').

claims.claim: THE ENERGY / 10,000+ years getting out
claims.note: Same lower bound as claim 12. Appears on the closing line after the cutaway has faded; the Sun-Earth shot is back with its own 'not to scale' label. A1: SOURCES item 2.

claims.claim: THE TRIP / 8 minutes to you / not to scale
claims.note: Same figure as claim 11. A1: SOURCES item 1.

claims.claim: Cutaway rings at 0.25 and 0.7 of the Sun's radius (core / radiative zone / convection zone).
claims.note: MSFC: core is 'the innermost 25%'; radiative zone 'from 25% of the distance to the surface to 70%'; convection zone 'the outermost 30%'. The 0.713 R from Christensen-Dalsgaard, Gough & Thompson 1991 was not opened (bibliographic details checked on Crossref) and is not needed: 0.7 rests on MSFC. A1: SOURCES item 6.

claims.claim: A random-walk path from the centre to the 0.7 ring, with short sideways strokes along it (absorption and re-emission).
claims.source_checked: NASA SVS 11084; NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior'; Mitalas & Sills 1992
claims.note: SVS: photons travel a 'drunken walk', 'absorbed by other atoms and emitted repeatedly'; MSFC: light 'bounces from particle to particle through the radiative zone'; MS92 model it as a random walk from the centre. The path stops at 0.7, where the sources hand transport to convection. Step size and the slight outward lean are schematic, and the cutaway is labelled 'not to scale' (claim 12). A1: SOURCES item 6.

claims.claim: Path coloured from violet toward pale yellow by log temperature: 15 MK at r=0, 7 MK at 0.25 R, 2 MK at 0.7 R, 5,700 K at the surface; ~10% of the way to yellow at 0.25 R and ~26% at 0.7 R.
claims.source_checked: NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior'; index.tsx (PROFILE and tint())
claims.note: MSFC gives ~15,000,000 C at the centre, 7,000,000 C falling to ~2,000,000 C across the radiative zone, and 5,700 K at the visible surface; the core-edge value ('half its central value', ~7.5 MK) is consistent with 7 MK. Recomputed: (ln 15e6 - ln 7e6)/(ln 15e6 - ln 5700) = 0.097, and for 2e6 = 0.256, matching the code and SOURCES. The hue is a schematic encoding, not the colour of X-rays, and SOURCES says so. A1: SOURCES item 6.

claims.claim: Rotating dashed convection cells between 0.7 R and the surface.
claims.source_checked: NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior'; Mitalas & Sills 1992 sec. 3
claims.note: MSFC: transport 'by convective fluid flows (boiling motion) through the convection zone, the outermost 30%'; 'These convective motions carry heat quite rapidly to the surface.' A1: SOURCES item 6.

claims.claim: A fan of five yellow rays leaving the surface.
claims.note: Depicts the energy leaving the surface as visible light (MSFC). A1: SOURCES items 4 and 6.

claims.claim: The energy in sunlight took at least tens of thousands of years to get out of the Sun
claims.note: The lowest figure from any source read is SVS's 40,000 yr; MS92 (1.7e5) and MSFC (~1e6) are higher, and MS92 call the lower textbook values (3e3-3e4) much too short. 'At least tens of thousands' matches the spoken hook; even the pedant's correction to MS92 in claim 1 (~2.8e4) stays in range. E2: the short pays this off.

claims.claim: Sunlight reaches you about eight minutes after leaving the Sun's surface.
claims.note: 496.7 s mean from the photosphere; 'about' is accurate.

claims.claim: But the energy it carries spent tens of thousands of years, maybe far more, getting out.
claims.note: Same as the spoken hook.

claims.claim: Estimates include about 40,000 years (NASA SVS), 170,000 (Mitalas & Sills 1992) and about a million (NASA Marshall).
claims.source_checked: NASA SVS 11084; Mitalas & Sills 1992 (ADS scan); NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior'
claims.note: SVS 'Over the course of 40,000 years'; MS92 't_d = 1.7 x 10^5 yr'; MSFC 'about a million years'. Each is attributed correctly. The end points differ (SVS: to the surface; MS92 and MSFC: to the base of the convection zone), but MS92 explicitly take that as the Sun's diffusion time scale because convection is much faster, so all three are fair 'getting out' estimates.

claims.claim: The slow part is the crawl through the Sun's radiative zone; convection then carries it quickly to the surface.
claims.source_checked: NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior'; Mitalas & Sills 1992 sec. 3 and Fig. 2
claims.note: MSFC puts the 'about a million years' in its radiative-zone paragraph and says convection carries heat 'quite rapidly to the surface'; MS92: the convective-zone crossing time is 'very much shorter' than the diffusion time. Pedant note, not a break: MS92 Fig. 2 puts roughly a third of their 1.7e5 yr inside 0.25 R, i.e. in the core, which is also radiative; the radiative zone is still the larger share, and the sentence contrasts radiative diffusion with convection. A1: SOURCES items 2 and 6.

claims.claim: Deep inside, it travels mostly as X-rays. It leaves as sunlight.
claims.note: Same as the spoken lines.

claims.claim: Source list: Mitalas & Sills 1992 ApJ 401, 759 doi:10.1086/172103; NASA Marshall interior page; NASA SVS 11084; Stix 2003 Solar Physics 212, 3 doi:10.1023/A:1022952621810; Christensen-Dalsgaard, Gough & Thompson 1991 ApJ 378, 413 doi:10.1086/170441; IAU 2012 Resolution B2; CODATA 2022.
claims.source_checked: Crossref API for the three DOIs (titles, journals, volumes, pages, years all match); NIST CODATA pages (labelled '2022 CODATA'); MSFC and SVS pages opened. Stix (Springer) and IAU not reachable; CDGT not opened.
claims.note: Bibliographic details are correct. But Stix 2003 is listed as a source with no caveat, although it was never read at source (SOURCES item 2 says so: 'not re-read at source'); A2 requires saying so, and nothing in the short or description rests on it ('maybe far more' is carried by MSFC's ~1e6 yr). Change: drop the Stix line from the description, or write it as 'Stix 2003, Solar Physics 212, 3 (not read at source)'.

claims.claim: Narration: Kokoro-82M synthetic voice. Illustrated animation; marked shots are not to scale.
claims.note: tts.py uses Kokoro-82M (Apache-2.0). Both non-to-scale visuals carry a 'not to scale' label while on screen: Earth's label for the Sun-Earth shot, and the '10,000+ YEARS' tag for the whole time the cutaway is visible.
